scope: Theorem 3.1 (Incidence criterion) of the manuscript “A Counterexample to Kaplansky's Direct-Finiteness Conjecture in Characteristic Two” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-Direct-Finiteness-Conjecture-in-Characteristic-Two-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 197 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a97d7915d43b5112), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime, let K be a finite field of characteristic two containing a primitive ℓth root of unity ζ, and put κ = ℓ2. Let V be a finite set of cardinality t, and let F be a finite family of nonempty subsets of V . Assume that every v ∈ V belongs to exactly ℓ + 1 members of F and that the bipartite incidence graph of V and F has girth at least 12. Suppose that an integer m and column vectors xv ∈ Km, v ∈ V , satisfy 0 < m < t ≤ mκ (3.1) and ∑︂ v∈V xvxT v = −Im, ∑︂ v∈f xvxT v = 0 for every f ∈ F. (3.2) Then there are a finitely presented group G containing an element of order ℓ and finite sums aout, bout ∈ K[G] such that aoutbout = 1, boutaout ̸= 1. They are given by the constructions and formulas below.
